questions.question: In a classroom activity, students pick up green and white cocktail sticks scattered across a lawn of green grass in 30 seconds. Which of the following best explains what this model demonstrates?
options: The cocktail sticks represent predators, and the green grass represents the camouflage of prey species.
The students act as predators, the sticks represent prey with different variations, and the grass is the environment.
The sticks represent nutrients in the soil, and the students represent plants competing to absorb them.
The students represent different species competing for the exact same nesting sites in a forest.

questions.question: In the cocktail stick model on green grass, students collect 80% of the white sticks but only 20% of the green sticks in the first round. If the surviving sticks are allowed to reproduce by adding more sticks of their own colour, what is the most reasonable prediction for the population over several generations?
options: The white sticks will eventually become more common because they are easier to find.
The total number of sticks will decrease to zero as students get faster at finding them.
The proportion of green sticks in the population will increase because they have a higher survival rate.
The ratio of green to white sticks will remain exactly 50:50 because reproduction is random.

questions.question: Imagine the lawn in the cocktail stick model suddenly becomes covered in a thick layer of white frost. How would this environmental change alter the predicted survival rates of the green and white sticks?
options: Green sticks would now be harder to find, so their survival rate would increase.
White sticks would become camouflaged against the frost, increasing their survival rate compared to green sticks.
Both green and white sticks would be collected at equal rates because frost has no effect on visibility.
The students would stop collecting sticks because the cold temperature would freeze the sticks in place.

questions.question: The fennec fox has exceptionally large ears. Which explanation best describes how this specific adaptation provides a survival advantage in its hot desert environment?
options: Large ears trap a layer of warm air close to the head to prevent the fox from shivering at night.
Large ears contain many blood vessels that allow excess body heat to radiate away, keeping the fox cool.
Large ears prevent sand from entering the inner ear canal during desert windstorms.
Large ears allow the fox to flap them to fly short distances over hot desert sand.

questions.question: Two species of birds feed on the same type of seed in a woodland. In a year with very low rainfall, the seed plants produce far fewer seeds than usual. What is the most likely outcome of this resource limitation?
options: The birds will voluntarily share the remaining seeds equally to ensure both species survive.
Both species will switch to eating leaves, completely eliminating any need to compete.
Competition for the limited seeds will increase, and the species less suited to finding or eating them may decrease in population.
The seeds will automatically grow larger and more nutritious to compensate for the low quantity.

questions.question: In a population of rabbits, some individuals have slightly longer, stronger hind legs than others. How does this variation affect their ability to compete and survive when a new predator enters their habitat?
options: All rabbits will instantly grow longer legs in response to seeing the predator.
Rabbits with longer legs can run faster to escape, making them more likely to survive and compete successfully.
The predator will only hunt rabbits with longer legs because they are more visible when running.
Leg length has no impact on survival because predators hunt entirely by scent.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes how natural selection leads to the evolution of a species over many generations?
options: Individual organisms decide to change their characteristics to suit their environment, then pass these new traits to their offspring.
The environment directly mutates the genes of every individual at the same time to make them better suited.
Individuals with advantageous traits are more likely to survive and reproduce, causing those traits to become more common over time.
Weak individuals are protected by stronger individuals, ensuring that all variations survive equally.

questions.question: In science, the term 'Theory of Evolution' is used. What does the word 'theory' mean in this scientific context?
options: An untested guess or hunch that has no supporting evidence.
A general explanation developed from a large body of evidence that explains many different observations.
A temporary idea that scientists use until they can find actual proof.
A rule of nature that can never be modified or updated by new discoveries.

questions.question: A population of bacteria is exposed to an antibiotic. A few bacteria survive because they have a feature that makes them resistant. Which statement correctly describes how this resistance arose?
options: The bacteria anticipated the antibiotic and consciously designed a protective shield.
The antibiotic caused the bacteria to intentionally mutate so they could survive.
A random genetic variation that happened to provide resistance was already present or appeared by chance, and was then selected for.
The bacteria evolved resistance because they needed it to survive, as evolution always plans ahead.

questions.question: A professional weightlifter trains hard for years and develops exceptionally large, strong muscles. Why is this change in the weightlifter's muscles not considered an example of evolution?
options: Evolution only occurs in plants and simple animals, not in humans.
The changes occurred within an individual's lifetime and do not change the genetic information passed to their offspring.
Muscle growth is a chemical change, whereas evolution only involves mechanical changes.
The weightlifter's children will automatically be born with giant muscles, which skips the process of natural selection.

questions.question: What is a fossil, scientifically speaking?
options: Any dead leaf or bone found lying on the forest floor today.
A preserved specimen kept in liquid alcohol by modern scientists in a lab.
The mineralised remains or traces of once-living organisms from long ago.
A synthetic replica of an ancient animal created using modern 3D-printing technology.

questions.question: Why must scientists be cautious when drawing conclusions about the complete history of life on Earth based only on fossil evidence?
options: Fossils cannot be dated using any scientific methods, so their age is entirely made up.
The fossil record is incomplete because soft-bodied organisms rarely fossilise, and many fossils have not been found or were destroyed.
Fossils only form from plants, so we have no fossil evidence of ancient animals.
Fossils constantly change their shapes while buried underground, making them unreliable.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of environmental variation rather than genetic variation in dogs?
options: A dog having a naturally curly coat of fur.
A dog having a scar on its ear from an old injury.
A dog having blue eyes instead of brown eyes.
A dog having a highly developed sense of smell due to its breed.

questions.question: A tree loses several of its branches during a severe lightning storm, leaving it permanently misshapen. If seeds from this tree are planted, what shape are the new saplings expected to grow into, and why?
options: They will grow misshapen because the parent tree's physical damage is passed down through its seeds.
They will grow into normal, fully-branched trees because environmental damage is not heritable.
They will grow with even fewer branches because the damage is amplified in the next generation.
They will fail to grow at all because damaged trees cannot produce functional seeds.

questions.question: Why can genetic variation, such as the instructions for growing sharp claws in tigers, be passed down to offspring, while a broken claw from an accident cannot?
options: Sharp claws are made of stronger cells that actively migrate to the reproductive organs.
Genetic variation is stored in DNA which is copied and passed to offspring, whereas physical injuries do not alter DNA.
Offspring choose which physical features they want to inherit from their parents after they are born.
Physical injuries are too small to be noticed by the cells that control reproduction.

questions.question: In a dry grassland, some plants have deeper root systems due to their genetic makeup. Why does this feature become more common in the population over several dry years?
options: The shallow-rooted plants decide to grow deeper roots in winter to prepare for the summer.
The deep-rooted plants survive the drought better, reproduce, and pass their genes for deep roots to their offspring.
The soil physically pulls the roots of all plants deeper to help them find water.
Deep roots are a dominant social trait that plants copy from their neighbors.

questions.question: During the Industrial Revolution in England, soot from coal burning blackened the bark of birch trees. How did this human-caused environmental change affect natural selection in the peppered moth population?
options: It caused all light-coloured moths to immediately mutate into dark-coloured moths within their lifetimes.
It gave dark-coloured moths a camouflage advantage on the dark soot-covered trees, making them more likely to survive and reproduce.
It made birds stop eating moths entirely because the soot made the moths taste bad.
It had no effect because natural selection is completely unaffected by human activities.

questions.question: According to scientific evidence, approximately when did the very first living organisms appear on Earth, and what type of organisms were they?
options: 4.5 billion years ago, and they were complex land plants.
3.8 billion years ago, and they were simple microorganisms.
500 million years ago, and they were ancient mammals.
10 thousand years ago, and they were modern humans.

questions.question: Based on scientific evidence, which of the following lists the correct chronological order of the appearance of these organisms on Earth, from oldest to most recent?
options: Mammals (200 million years ago) to Land plants (500 million years ago) to Modern humans (350 thousand years ago)
Land plants (500 million years ago) to Mammals (200 million years ago) to Modern humans (350 thousand years ago)
Modern humans (350 thousand years ago) to Mammals (200 million years ago) to Land plants (500 million years ago)
Land plants (500 million years ago) to Modern humans (350 thousand years ago) to Mammals (200 million years ago)

questions.question: Why do scientists divide the 4.5 billion-year history of the Earth into specific blocks of time called eons, periods, and epochs?
options: To keep the history of Earth secret from the general public.
Because the Earth's orbit changes shape exactly every time a new period begins.
To make this vast span of time easier to study, understand, and organize based on major geological and biological events.
Because these are the names of the ancient scientists who originally discovered the Earth.

questions.question: In a simulation of natural selection, students use tweezers to pick up green and white cocktail sticks from green grass within a 30-second time limit. Why does this model serve as a demonstration of natural selection?
options: The tweezers represent a predator, and the cocktail sticks represent prey where camouflage determines survival chance.
The tweezers represent the prey, and the cocktail sticks represent different food types available to them.
The experiment shows how individuals can choose to change their color to match their surroundings.
The cocktail sticks represent different species that cooperate with each other to avoid being picked up.

questions.question: In a classroom experiment, students repeatedly pick colored cocktail sticks from green grass. Over five rounds, they record the remaining sticks and "reproduce" them by adding matching colors. What prediction can be made about the population's composition over time?
options: The population will become entirely white sticks because they are more visible.
The proportion of green sticks will increase because they are harder for "predators" to see and remove.
The total number of sticks will decrease to zero as all colors are equally likely to be eliminated.
The proportions of green and white sticks will remain completely equal due to random selection.

questions.question: A classroom simulation uses green and white cocktail sticks on a green lawn to represent prey. If a sudden snowfall covers the lawn, making the ground white, how does this change the prediction for the population over time?
options: Green sticks will now have a survival advantage, so their proportion will increase.
White sticks will now have a survival advantage, so their proportion will increase.
Both colors will be picked at the exact same rate because color no longer affects visibility.
The predators will stop feeding because they cannot see any cocktail sticks.

questions.question: Marram grass is a plant that grows on dry, windy sand dunes. It has rolled leaves with hairs on the inside and stomata sunk into pits. What is the primary purpose of these specific leaf adaptations?
options: To trap a layer of moist air and reduce water loss by transpiration.
To absorb nitrogen gas directly from the strong sea winds.
To reflect sunlight so the plant can maintain a freezing temperature.
To catch falling rain and channel it directly to the outer roots.

questions.question: Polar bears have thick layers of blubber and white-looking fur. How do these adaptations work together to provide an advantage in their specific Arctic environment?
options: The blubber protects them from being seen by prey, while the white fur stores water.
The white fur provides camouflage against the ice for hunting, while the blubber reduces heat loss in freezing temperatures.
The blubber helps them swim faster than fish, while the white fur absorbs maximum solar radiation to overheat them.
The white fur attracts mates from long distances, while the blubber allows them to digest ice.

questions.question: Red squirrels and grey squirrels both live in the same British woodlands. Why does a lack of hazelnuts in autumn lead to intense competition between them?
options: Hazelnuts are a limited resource, meaning there are not enough to satisfy the survival needs of both populations.
Hazelnuts are poisonous to grey squirrels, so red squirrels must eat them all to protect them.
One species will voluntarily stop eating to allow the other species to survive.
Hazelnuts are an unlimited resource, but the squirrels prefer to fight rather than share.

questions.question: Bluebell plants growing on a deciduous forest floor flower very early in spring, before the tall oak trees grow their new leaves. Which resource are the bluebells primarily competing for by timing their growth this way?
options: Soil nutrients
Pollinators
Light
Space for roots

questions.question: In a population of desert plants, some individuals have slightly deeper root systems than others due to natural variation. During a severe, multi-year drought, what is the most likely outcome of this variation?
options: All the plants will survive equally because they belong to the same species.
Plants with shallower roots will grow deeper roots overnight to adapt to the drought.
Plants with deeper roots will access deep water tables, making them more successful competitors for survival.
The plants with deeper roots will dry out faster because they have to pump water a longer distance.

questions.question: How does natural selection lead to the evolution of a species over many generations?
options: It causes individual organisms to intentionally mutate their own genes to suit the environment.
It ensures that only the weakest individuals survive, making more resources available for offspring.
It causes advantageous characteristics to become more common in the population over time as survivors pass them on.
It guarantees that every single offspring born will have identical, perfect features from birth.

questions.question: In science, why is the "theory of evolution by natural selection" classified as a scientific theory?
options: It is an untested hunch that scientists use when they lack physical evidence.
It is a general explanation, developed from vast evidence, that explains many different biological observations.
It is a temporary guess that will be replaced once a single fossil is found.
It is an absolute, unchanging law that was proven without needing any observations.

questions.question: An island has no fruit-eating birds. A storm blows a population of insect-eating birds onto the island, where there are many fruiting trees but few insects. Which statement best explains how a fruit-eating beak could emerge in this population?
options: The birds will consciously decide to change their beak shapes so they do not starve.
Random genetic mutations may produce a bird with a beak slightly better suited for fruit, which natural selection then maintains.
The environment forces all the birds to simultaneously develop wider beaks within their lifetimes.
The trees will mutate their fruits to have softer skins so the insect-eating birds can eat them.

questions.question: An individual green lizard loses its tail to a predator but survives. It later grows a slightly shorter, tougher tail made of cartilage. Why is this change not considered an example of evolution?
options: Because evolution only occurs in plants, not in vertebrates like lizards.
Because changes in the features of an individual within its lifetime do not represent evolution of the species.
Because the lizard did not lose its tail due to a natural predator.
Because the new tail is stronger than the old tail, and evolution only makes features weaker.

questions.question: A student finds a rock containing a clear imprint of an ancient fern leaf. Which statement correctly describes the nature of this fossil?
options: It is the actual, original organic leaf tissue preserved without any chemical change.
It is a mineralised trace or remain of a once-living organism.
It is a synthetic replica created by modern geologists to simulate ancient life.
It is a non-organic rock pattern formed purely by volcanic heat with no connection to living things.

questions.question: Why must scientists be cautious when drawing conclusions about ancient ecosystems based solely on the fossil record?
options: Organisms with soft bodies rarely form fossils, meaning the fossil record is incomplete and biased toward hard-bodied species.
Fossils can only form in areas that have never experienced geological changes.
Fossil evidence is entirely subjective and cannot be analyzed using scientific methods.
All organisms that ever lived have been fossilized, making the record too large to analyze.

questions.question: Two genetically identical twin plants are grown in different conditions. Plant A is grown in fertile soil with abundant sunlight and grows tall. Plant B is grown in poor soil with low light and remains stunted. What caused this variation?
options: Genetic variation, because their DNA sequences changed to match their environments.
Environmental variation, because their differences are due to external conditions and resources.
Evolutionary adaptation, because Plant B chose to stay small to avoid being seen.
Artificial selection, because a breeder actively chose which plant should be tall.

questions.question: A dog trainer spends years working with an athletic dog, building up its muscle mass and teaching it complex agility tricks. If this dog later breeds, which of these traits can be passed on to its offspring?
options: The increased muscle mass, because physical training alters the genetic code in the reproductive cells.
The specific agility tricks, because learned behaviors are automatically written into DNA.
Neither the trained muscle mass nor the learned tricks, because environmental variation is not heritable.
Both the muscle mass and the tricks, because all characteristics acquired in life are inherited.

questions.question: A scientist studies a population of beetles. Some have genes that code for bright green shells, while others have genes for brown shells. Why is this genetic variation significant for natural selection?
options: It is not heritable, so it will disappear when the current generation dies.
It is heritable, meaning the shell color instructions can be passed on to offspring, allowing the population to adapt over generations.
It allows the beetles to change their shell color at will depending on the predator nearby.
It guarantees that both colors will always exist in equal numbers regardless of environmental changes.

questions.question: In a cold environment, rabbits with thicker fur are better able to survive the winter than rabbits with thin fur. Why does this lead to a change in the rabbit population over time?
options: The thin-furred rabbits will migrate to a warm desert, leaving only thick-furred rabbits behind.
The surviving thick-furred rabbits are more likely to reproduce and pass their heritable fur-thickness genes to their offspring.
The cold weather directly mutates the genes of the thin-furred rabbits to make their offspring have thick fur.
Rabbits with thin fur will decide to stop reproducing to save resources for others.

questions.question: During the Industrial Revolution in England, soot from coal burning coated the trunks of birch trees, turning them dark. How did this human-induced environmental change affect natural selection in the peppered moth population?
options: It caused dark-colored moths to become easier for predators to spot, reducing their numbers.
It gave dark-colored moths a camouflage advantage over light-colored moths, increasing their survival and reproduction.
It forced light-colored moths to instantly dye their wings dark to survive.
It stopped natural selection from occurring because humans had taken control of the environment.

questions.question: According to scientific evidence, which of the following lists evolutionary milestones in the correct chronological order, from oldest to most recent?
options: First land plants (500 mya) -> First mammals (200 mya) -> Modern humans (350k years ago)
Modern humans (350k years ago) -> First mammals (200 mya) -> First land plants (500 mya)
First mammals (200 mya) -> First land plants (500 mya) -> Modern humans (350k years ago)
First land plants (500 mya) -> Modern humans (350k years ago) -> First mammals (200 mya)

questions.question: In a classroom simulation, students scatter 50 green and 50 white cocktail sticks on a green lawn. They have 15 seconds to pick up as many as possible. Which of the following best explains why the white sticks are collected much faster than the green ones?
options: The green sticks are physically heavier and harder to pick up.
The green sticks are camouflaged against the green grass, making them harder for the collectors to see.
The white sticks are stickier and cling to the students' fingers.
Students naturally prefer the colour white and choose to ignore the green sticks.

questions.question: If the green and white cocktail stick simulation on a green lawn is repeated after a heavy snowfall that completely covers the grass in white, how would the survival prediction for each stick colour change?
options: Green sticks will now be collected faster because they stand out against the white snow.
White sticks will still be collected faster because snow does not affect human vision.
Both stick colours will be collected at exactly the same rate because snow makes them equally visible.
Neither stick will be collected because the snow will melt the cocktail sticks.

questions.question: Some desert plants have very shallow, widespread root systems rather than deep taproots. How does this particular adaptation provide an advantage in a dry desert environment?
options: It allows the plant to anchor itself deeply into bedrock to avoid being blown away.
It enables the plant to quickly absorb scarce water from light rainfall before it evaporates.
It helps the plant find underground water tables deep below the surface.
It prevents the plant from absorbing too much mineral salt from the lower soil layers.

questions.question: A gardener plants 100 lettuce seeds very close together in a tiny pot. After a few weeks, only a few seedlings grow large, while the rest wither and die. Which ecological concept best explains this outcome?
options: The seedlings are cooperating to share the limited soil space equally.
The seeds had different genetic plans to sprout at different times of the year.
Limited resources like light, water, and space led to intense competition where only some survived.
The soil automatically selected the seeds with the darkest green leaves to grow.

questions.question: In a forest of tall trees, some individual giraffes are born with slightly longer necks than others of the same species. During a severe drought where lower leaves are eaten, how does this variation affect competition?
options: It forces the longer-necked giraffes to migrate to find water elsewhere.
It gives longer-necked individuals a competitive advantage by allowing them to reach food others cannot.
It causes the shorter-necked giraffes to quickly grow longer necks within their lifetime.
It makes the longer-necked giraffes more visible to predators, leading to their rapid extinction.

questions.question: Which statement best describes what a 'scientific theory' is, in the context of the theory of evolution by natural selection?
options: An educated guess made by a scientist that has not yet been tested or supported by evidence.
A permanent, unchangeable law of nature that requires no further observation or refinement.
A general explanation developed from extensive evidence that explains many different observed examples.
A personal opinion shared by a group of scientists about how organisms might have looked in the past.

questions.question: A common misconception is that organisms consciously decide to evolve new features to survive environmental changes. Which of the following correctly describes how advantageous features actually arise?
options: They appear randomly due to genetic variation and are then maintained by natural selection if they provide a benefit.
They are planned in advance by the species so they can prepare for future climates.
They are directly caused by the organism's physical effort to stretch or strengthen its body.
They are injected into the organisms by their parents during their developmental stages.

questions.question: A professional weightlifter trains intensely and develops exceptionally large muscles. If this weightlifter has children, how will their muscles be affected at birth, and why?
options: The children will be born with exceptionally large muscles because evolution occurs within a single lifetime.
The children will not be born with large muscles because changes in an individual's features during their lifetime are not evolutionary and cannot be passed on.
The children will have large muscles only if they are born in the same gym environment.
The children will have slightly larger muscles because the parent's exercise modified their genetic code permanently.

questions.question: A student discovers a rock containing the fossilised footprint of an ancient dinosaur. How should this fossil be scientifically classified?
options: It is not a true fossil because it does not contain actual preserved bones or teeth.
It is a fossil because it is a mineralised trace left behind by a once-living organism.
It is an artificial carving made by early humans to record dinosaur sightings.
It is a preserved piece of actual dinosaur skin that has dried out over millions of years.

questions.question: Why is it difficult for scientists to reconstruct a complete, perfect history of all past life on Earth using only fossil evidence?
options: Fossils only form in places with active volcanoes, leaving most habitats unrepresented.
Most dead organisms decay completely or are eaten, so only a small fraction ever become fossilised.
Fossils can only show the exact colours and soft internal organs of ancient creatures, not their bones.
Scientific equipment is currently unable to determine the age of any fossil older than ten thousand years.

questions.question: An oak tree loses several large branches during a severe storm, leaving it permanently scarred and misshapen. If acorns from this tree are planted, what features should we expect the new oak trees to have?
options: They will grow up misshapen and missing branches because the parent's injury is passed down.
They will grow up normal because environmental damage is not heritable and cannot be passed to offspring.
They will grow up extra strong to prevent future storm damage, as trees plan for the future.
They will fail to grow at all because injured trees only produce infertile seeds.

questions.question: A species of rabbit has genetic instructions that cause some individuals to have thick fur and others to have thin fur. How does this type of variation behave across generations?
options: It is entirely determined by how much the parent rabbits exercise during their lifetimes.
It is environmental, meaning thick-furred rabbits will have thin-furred offspring if the weather gets warmer.
It is heritable, meaning the genetic instructions for fur thickness can be passed from parents to offspring.
It cannot be passed on because physical features are only determined by the soil and water conditions.

questions.question: In a cold environment, birds with dense downy feathers survive winter much better than birds with thin feathers. Over several generations, what is the most likely outcome for this bird population?
options: The proportion of thin-feathered birds will increase as they try harder to stay warm.
The average density of feathers will decrease because resources are too scarce to grow them.
Dense downy feathers will become more common because the survivors pass this heritable feature to their offspring.
The birds will stop reproducing entirely to conserve energy during the cold winter months.

questions.question: During the Industrial Revolution, soot from coal factories blackened the trunks of nearby birch trees. How did this human activity affect the natural selection of light-coloured and dark-coloured peppered moths?
options: It had no effect because moths do not rely on tree trunks for survival.
It changed the selective pressure, making dark moths less visible to predators and more likely to survive and reproduce.
It forced light-coloured moths to instantly change their DNA to turn dark during their lifetime.
It caused all moths to stop reproducing until the soot washed away.

questions.question: A geologist is organizing a museum display of fossils. Based on scientific evidence, what are the approximate ages of the oldest and newest fossils found on Earth?
options: Oldest are 4.5 billion years old; newest are 1 billion years old.
Oldest are 3.5 billion years old; newest are around 10 thousand years old.
Oldest are 200 million years old; newest are 350 thousand years old.
Oldest are 500 million years old; newest are 200 years old.

questions.question: According to scientific evidence, which of the following lists the evolutionary appearance of organisms in the correct chronological order, from the oldest event to the most recent?
options: First mammals (200mya) -> First land plants (500mya) -> Modern humans (350k years ago)
First land plants (500mya) -> First mammals (200mya) -> Modern humans (350k years ago)
Modern humans (350k years ago) -> First mammals (200mya) -> First land plants (500mya)
First land plants (500mya) -> Modern humans (350k years ago) -> First mammals (200mya)

questions.question: Emperor penguins live in the freezing environment of the Antarctic. Which of the following is a physical feature that directly suits them to survive this extreme cold?
options: A thick layer of blubber under their skin to trap heat.
Brightly coloured feathers to attract warm sunlight.
Long, hollow legs that keep their bodies far above the ice.
Wide, thin wings designed for rapid flight through cold winds.

questions.question: Two different species of flowering plants grow in the same meadow. Both rely on the same species of bumblebee to transfer their pollen. In this scenario, what specific resource are these two plant species competing for?
options: Seed dispersers to carry their seeds away.
Shelter from harsh winds and heavy rain.
Pollinators to enable successful reproduction.
Mates of the same species to produce offspring.

questions.question: A puppy is born with a perfectly healthy tail, but unfortunately loses its tail in an accident when it is young. What type of variation does this taillessness represent?
options: Genetic variation, because it is an instruction stored in the dog's DNA.
Environmental variation, because it was caused by an event in the dog's life rather than its genes.
Heritable variation, because its future puppies will also be born without tails.
Evolutionary variation, because the entire species is adapting to have no tails.

questions.question: When discussing the timeline of life and evolution, scientists refer to the age of the Earth. According to scientific evidence, approximately when was the Earth formed?
options: 4.5 million years ago
3.8 billion years ago
4.5 billion years ago
10 thousand years ago

questions.question: In a simulation of natural selection, students use tweezers to pick up green and white cocktail sticks from a green lawn in a set amount of time. What does this simulation demonstrate about predators and prey?
options: Predators have to learn how to change their color to match their surroundings.
White sticks are easier to see, representing how camouflaged prey are less likely to be eaten.
Green sticks will eventually mutate into white sticks to avoid being eaten.
Both green and white sticks have an equal chance of survival because predators hunt by smell.

questions.question: Using the green and white cocktail stick model on a green lawn over several generations (where survivors reproduce by adding another stick of their own color), what is the predicted change in the population?
options: The proportion of green sticks will increase while the proportion of white sticks will decrease.
The population will reach an exact 50/50 balance of green and white sticks.
White sticks will develop green stripes to survive better.
Both populations will decrease to zero because predators become more efficient.

questions.question: If the lawn in the cocktail stick model becomes heavily covered in frost and snow, how would this environmental change affect the prediction of which sticks survive?
options: Green sticks would become easier to see and would be picked up more, causing white sticks to become more common.
Predators would no longer be able to see any sticks, so both types would survive equally.
White sticks would try to turn green to blend back into the grass underneath.
The frosty ground would protect the green sticks from being picked up.

questions.question: Many desert plants have very deep root systems. What is this specific adaptation and its primary purpose?
options: Thick waxy leaves to store water from the air.
Deep roots to tap into underground water supplies far below the surface.
Spines to prevent water loss from the stem during the night.
Shallow roots to collect overnight dew quickly before it evaporates.

questions.question: How does the thick layer of blubber in a seal provide an advantage in its cold marine environment?
options: It increases their surface-area-to-volume ratio so they can absorb heat from the sun.
It helps them sink faster to the ocean floor to escape predators.
It provides insulation to reduce heat loss, keeping their internal temperature stable in freezing water.
It stores oxygen so they can remain underwater for several days without breathing.

questions.question: Why does competition occur between individuals of the same species in a forest?
options: Because they want to share resources to ensure the entire species survives.
Because resources like space and nutrients are limited, and not every individual can get enough.
Because individuals are programmed to fight to keep their population from growing too large.
Because different species always cooperate, leaving only members of the same species to compete.

questions.question: Plants in a dense woodland often grow very tall and have broad leaves. Which limited resource are they primarily competing for?
options: Pollinators
Oxygen
Light
Seed dispersers

questions.question: In a dry season, some individual giraffes have slightly longer necks than others of the same species. How does this variation affect their ability to compete?
options: The longer-necked giraffes can reach food higher up that others cannot, making them more competitive.
The shorter-necked giraffes can run faster, allowing them to find water holes first.
All giraffes are equally successful because they share the available leaves at all heights.
The longer-necked giraffes will share their food with the shorter-necked giraffes to preserve the herd.

questions.question: How does natural selection lead to the evolution of a species over many generations?
options: Individuals change their own features when needed, and then pass these newly acquired features to their offspring.
Organisms with advantageous characteristics are more likely to survive and reproduce, making those traits more common over time.
The environment forces organisms to mutate in a specific, helpful direction to survive.
A species decides to change its characteristics to avoid competing with other species.

questions.question: In science, what is the best definition of a scientific theory, such as the theory of evolution by natural selection?
options: A temporary guess made by a scientist before any experiments are carried out.
An idea that has been proven absolutely true and can never be questioned or modified.
A general explanation developed from a large body of evidence that explains many different observations.
An opinion held by the majority of the public about how a natural process works.

questions.question: Which of the following statements best describes how new advantageous features arise in a population?
options: They are planned in advance by the species to prepare for future climate changes.
They appear randomly due to genetic changes, and are then preserved because they help the organism survive.
They are created by the environment directly modifying the DNA of organisms to help them.
They only appear when a species is in danger of immediate extinction.

questions.question: An individual dog loses a leg in an accident but learns to run very quickly on three legs. Why is this change not considered evolution?
options: Because evolution only occurs in plants, not in mammals.
Because the change occurred during its lifetime and does not alter its genetic code to be passed to offspring.
Because running on three legs is not an advantage for survival.
Because evolution only happens when the entire population changes at the exact same second.

questions.question: Which of the following would be correctly classified as a fossil under scientific definitions?
options: A preserved modern leaf that fell from a tree last autumn.
The mineralised remains of a dinosaur bone or a preserved footprint left in hardened mud.
A piece of plastic trash that has been buried in sand for ten years.
An injured animal that has been stuffed and preserved by a taxidermist.

questions.question: What is a major limitation when scientists try to draw conclusions about ancient life solely from fossil evidence?
options: Fossils cannot be found in sedimentary rocks, which are the most common rocks on Earth.
Soft-bodied organisms rarely form fossils, meaning the fossil record is incomplete and biased towards hard parts.
Fossils only show the behavior of animals, never their physical shapes or structures.
No fossils have ever been found that are older than one million years.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of variation caused entirely by the environment or lifestyle rather than genetics?
options: Having blue eyes.
Developing large muscles through regular weightlifting.
Having naturally curly hair.
The biological sex of a mammal.

questions.question: A person trains hard and becomes a champion runner, developing a very efficient cardiovascular system. Why will their future children not be born with this same level of athletic training?
options: Because athletic ability is a dominant genetic trait that skips a generation.
Because environmental variations and acquired lifestyle traits are not heritable.
Because the children's body cells will actively reject any traits gained from exercise.
Because training only affects the reproductive cells and not the rest of the body.

questions.question: Why can genetic variation, such as a bird having a sharper beak shape, be passed down through generations?
options: Because it is caused by genetic information which is copied and inherited by offspring.
Because the parents teach the offspring how to sharpen their beaks on rocks.
Because the food the bird eats directly rewrites its beak genes every day.
Because all physical traits are passed on regardless of whether they are genetic or environmental.

questions.question: According to the theory of natural selection, what makes an individual organism fit in its environment, and what is the consequence?
options: Being the strongest and most aggressive, which allows it to live forever.
Having features well-suited to the environment, making it more likely to survive, reproduce, and pass on its genes.
Being able to change its genetic code at will to match any sudden environmental changes.
Having the largest number of mutations, regardless of whether they are helpful or harmful.

questions.question: How might human-induced air pollution that darkens tree trunks with soot affect the natural selection of a moth species with both light and dark varieties?
options: The light moths will instantly mutate to become dark to save themselves.
Dark moths will become better camouflaged, survive longer, and become more common in the population.
The moths will stop reproducing until the trees become clean again.
Both varieties will die out immediately because moths cannot survive on dark trees.

questions.question: Based on scientific evidence of Earth's history, which of the following lists the appearance of organisms in the correct chronological order, from oldest to most recent?
options: Land plants (500mya), Mammals (200mya), Modern humans (350kya)
Modern humans (350kya), Mammals (200mya), Land plants (500mya)
Mammals (200mya), Land plants (500mya), Modern humans (350kya)
Land plants (500mya), Modern humans (350kya), Mammals (200mya)
